chapters.name: Microbiology and Infection Control
chapters.summary: Types of germs, and the difference between sanitation, disinfection, and sterilization.
keyPoints: Sanitation cleans to reduce germs; disinfection kills most germs; sterilization kills all microbial life, including spores.
Clean a tool first, because a disinfectant works only on a clean surface.
Porous items such as cotton pads and emery boards are single-use.
Treat all blood and body fluids as possibly infectious (Standard Precautions).

chapters.name: Anatomy and Physiology
chapters.summary: Cells, tissues, the layers of the skin, and the muscles and nerves of the face.
keyPoints: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form body systems.
The epidermis is the outer layer; the dermis holds blood vessels, nerves, and glands.
Melanin gives skin its color and helps protect it from UV light.
The trigeminal nerve is the chief sensory nerve of the face.

chapters.name: Skin Disorders and Diseases
chapters.summary: Glands, lesions, contagious conditions, pigment disorders, growths, and skin cancers.
keyPoints: Sebaceous glands make oil; sudoriferous glands make sweat.
Primary lesions (macule, papule, vesicle, pustule) come first; secondary lesions (crust, scale, scar) follow.
Tinea, impetigo, and scabies are contagious.
Basal cell carcinoma is the most common skin cancer; melanoma is the most dangerous.

chapters.name: Hair, Electricity, and Safety
chapters.summary: Hair structure and growth, electrical basics, and safe use of equipment and chemicals.
keyPoints: A hair has three layers: cuticle, cortex, and medulla.
The growth cycle is anagen (growth), catagen (transition), and telogen (rest).
A volt measures pressure, an ampere measures current, and an ohm measures resistance.
A Safety Data Sheet (SDS) explains a chemical's hazards and handling.

chapters.name: Consultation and Skin Analysis
chapters.summary: Client intake, health history, skin types, the Fitzpatrick scale, and when to refer a client.
keyPoints: Use an intake form and consultation to learn health history, products, and goals.
Skin types include normal, dry, oily, combination, and sensitive; dehydrated skin lacks water.
The Fitzpatrick scale groups skin by how it reacts to sun, from Type I to Type VI.
Do not diagnose; refer clients with a medical concern to a physician.

chapters.name: Facial Treatments and Exfoliation
chapters.summary: Steps of a facial, steaming, massage movements, masks, and chemical and mechanical exfoliation.
keyPoints: A facial starts with cleansing and ends with moisturizer and sunscreen.
The massage movements are effleurage, petrissage, friction, tapotement, and vibration.
AHAs and BHAs are chemical exfoliants; microdermabrasion and scrubs are mechanical.
Steam softens the skin but should be limited on couperose or rosacea skin.

chapters.name: Hair Removal, Lash, and Brow
chapters.summary: Waxing, tweezing, depilatories, and eyebrow and eyelash services.
keyPoints: Epilation removes hair from the root; depilation removes it at the surface.
Apply wax with hair growth and remove it against growth, parallel to the skin.
Do a patch test before tinting lashes or brows.
Skip waxing on sunburned, irritated, or fragile skin.

chapters.name: Makeup, Products, and Ingredients
chapters.summary: Color basics, makeup hygiene, sun protection, and common skin care ingredients.
keyPoints: Primary colors are red, yellow, and blue; complementary colors sit opposite each other.
Humectants draw water in; occlusives hold it in.
Broad-spectrum sunscreen protects against UVA and UVB.
Never share or re-dip makeup applicators between clients.
